newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori's ex-wife calls for brother's release.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori's ex-wife calls for brother's release.

text.p: The former wife of President Alberto Fujimori appealed to Marxist rebels on Friday to release his younger brother, one of 73 hostages being held inside the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"I want to stress to them (the rebels) that Pedro Fujimori came to Peru to help the poor," former first lady Susana Higuchi told CPN local radio.
"These are ideals which I believe you (the rebels) also share," she said.

Using emotional, personal words, Higuchi then spoke as if she were directly addressing her former husband's brother, who was captured by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) gunmen at a cocktail party at the residence on Dec. 17.
"You are a positive and good man ... Your wife and children, my children and myself miss you very much. Take care. We love you very much," she said.
Fujimori divorced Higuchi in 1995 following a bitter separation during which he locked her out of the presidential home after she accused him of corruption and authoritarianism.
Pedro Fujimori, who like his brother is the son of Japanese immigrants, is a low-profile member of the first family and has spent some time out of the country.
